A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PALU research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–I. Text extraction and rendered inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v3 reports original TOFU and MUSE experiments, ablations, model-scale analyses, and generated-response examples.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: PALU's token selection, reference-model top-K selection, losses, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Replacing 'vocabulary tokens' with 'output tokens' in Section 4.2 clarifies terminology without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same TOFU coverage and MUSE News and Books tasks. No training or evaluation dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the TOFU and MUSE experiments, convergence comparison, and generation examples. Appendix F.3 corrects a comparator's name in the discussion without changing the evaluated methods.

E3.justification: The reported splits, model sizes, training budgets, ablation settings, and testing procedures are retained. Section 5.7 clarifies the existing Table 2 evaluation without reporting changed score computations or experimental settings.

E4.justification: The top-K, prefix-length, target-value, token-position, and truncation-ratio analyses are unchanged, as are convergence plots, 13B experiments, dataset analyses, and generation case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same KS-test-based Forget Quality metric and statistical reporting practices. Neither adds run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical results are unchanged, but Table 1 corrects the second-best Llama-3.1-8B R-TR marking from SimNPO's 0.4726 to DPO's 0.4794. Appendix F.3 corrects PALU's News KnowMem comparison: its 0.4442 is below Original's 0.6443, not Retain's 0.3279.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, complexity analysis, and Appendix A derivations are unchanged. Revising the description of an empirical Retain score does not alter a formal bound or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about localized entropy maximization, sparse intervention, efficiency, and the forgetting–utility trade-off.

C2.justification: Section 5.7 replaces the claim of stronger privacy than retraining with an interpretation of low directional AUC as strong target suppression that need not match Retain's distribution. Section 5.2 also replaces 'theoretical upper bound' with 'Retain model reference score.' These qualify specific interpretations while preserving the broader explanation.

D1.justification: Section 5.7 newly identifies the existing Table 2 scores as directional AUCs measuring separability between forget and holdout samples. Hardware, training settings, hyperparameter searches, annotation procedures, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are unchanged. Bibliography differences reflect text flowing across page boundaries, not added or removed references.

P1.justification: Section 5.7 receives a localized rewrite, with additional wording corrections in Sections 4.2, 5.2, and Appendix F.3. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 is enlarged and loses its downward arrows, ranking emphasis, and best/second-best caption statement. Table 4 loses result emphasis, and Table 1 corrects an underline. Subsequent text reflows; figures and table membership remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the accuracy of conclusions drawn from unchanged evidence: Section 5.7 withdraws the stronger-privacy-than-retraining inference, Section 5.2 stops calling an empirical score a theoretical bound, and Table 1 and Appendix F.3 correct comparisons. These are useful, focused corrections rather than a substantial revision of the paper's overall scientific support.
